Solar geometry at the overpass time

Source: R/solar-geometry.R
ef_solar_geometry.Rd

Computes, for each pixel and its overpass instant, the position of the sun relative to the horizontal and to the tilted plane of the pixel: the cosine of the solar zenith angle, the cosine of the solar incidence angle on the pixel plane, the solar declination, the hour angle and the inverse relative Earth-Sun distance. These are the geometric inputs of the shortwave transmissivity (ef_tau_sw()) and of the incoming shortwave radiation (ef_rs_in()).

Usage

ef_solar_geometry(doy, utc_hour, lat, lon, slope = 0, aspect = 0)

Arguments

doy

Numeric. Day of year of the UTC date of the instant [-]: a whole number in 1-366.

utc_hour

Numeric. UTC time of day of the instant [h], decimal hours in [0, 24). It must be a UTC time (see Details).

lat

Numeric. Latitude [rad], in [-pi/2, pi/2] (pixel centre, WGS84).

lon

Numeric. Longitude [rad], positive east, in [-pi, pi].

slope

Numeric. Slope of the pixel plane [rad], in [0, pi/2]. Default 0 (horizontal plane).

aspect

Numeric. Aspect of the pixel plane [rad], GIS convention (clockwise from geographic north: 0 north, pi/2 east, pi south, 3 pi/2 west), in [0, 2 pi). Default 0; irrelevant when slope = 0, but an NA aspect still propagates (decision RC-16).

Value

A plain list (no class) of numeric vectors, all with the common length of the inputs and, if the inputs include matrices or arrays, their common dim:

  • cos_zenith: cosine of the solar zenith angle on the horizontal \(\cos\theta_h\) [-];

  • cos_incidence: cosine of the solar incidence angle on the pixel plane \(\cos\theta_{rel}\) [-];

  • declination: solar declination \(\delta\) [rad];

  • hour_angle: hour angle \(\omega\) [rad], in [-pi, pi), negative in the morning;

  • inv_distance: inverse relative Earth-Sun distance \(d_r\) [-].

Values of cos_zenith or cos_incidence \(\le 0\) (sun below the horizon, or plane facing away from the sun) are returned unchanged: their treatment belongs to the consuming functions.

Details

With \(J\) = doy, \(\phi\) = lat, \(\lambda\) = lon, \(s\) = slope and \(A\) = aspect: $$\delta = 0.409 \sin\left(\frac{2\pi J}{365} - 1.39\right), \quad d_r = 1 + 0.033 \cos\left(\frac{2\pi J}{365}\right)$$ $$b = \frac{2\pi (J - 81)}{364}, \quad S_c = 0.1645 \sin 2b - 0.1255 \cos b - 0.025 \sin b$$ $$t_s = \left(t_{UTC} + \frac{12}{\pi}\lambda + S_c\right) \bmod 24, \quad \omega = \frac{\pi}{12}(t_s - 12)$$ $$\cos\theta_h = \sin\delta \sin\phi + \cos\delta \cos\phi \cos\omega$$ and, with \(\gamma = A - \pi\) (surface azimuth: 0 facing south, east negative, west positive), $$\cos\theta_{rel} = \sin\delta \sin\phi \cos s - \sin\delta \cos\phi \sin s \cos\gamma + \cos\delta \cos\phi \cos s \cos\omega + \cos\delta \sin\phi \sin s \cos\gamma \cos\omega + \cos\delta \sin\gamma \sin s \sin\omega$$ which reduces to \(\cos\theta_h\) when \(s = 0\).

Time. The equation of time \(S_c\) is applied exactly once, here. utc_hour must therefore be a UTC time. The daytime view time of MODIS MOD11A1/MYD11A1 is local mean solar time (UTC plus the longitude in degrees divided by 15) and must be converted to UTC first, as \(t_{UTC} = (t_{ls} - \lambda_{deg}/15) \bmod 24\), with doy the day of year of the UTC date of the file. A local apparent solar time must not be converted this way: the equation of time would be applied twice. The declination and \(d_r\) are evaluated at the UTC date, which can differ by one day from the local solar date.

Angles are in radians throughout (decision RC-01). A latitude given in degrees by mistake (e.g. -35) lies outside [-pi/2, pi/2] and raises an error; a small slope given in degrees (e.g. 1) cannot be detected.

Assumptions: low-precision calendar formulae of FAO-56, with the same 365-day expressions in leap years; no atmospheric refraction; only self-shading is represented (no cast shadows from surrounding relief, and no reduction of the sky view by the horizon).

Arguments must be numeric and have length 1 or a common length; length-1 arguments are recycled, matrix or array arguments must share their dim. A non-integer doy raises earthflux_input_error; values outside the domains above, or infinite values, raise earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error). Missing values propagate to the outputs that depend on them.

Verification status

The declination, the inverse relative distance, the equation of time and the hour angle are VERIFICADA against FAO-56 (chapter 3, Eqs. 23, 24 and 31-33; the hour angle is Eq. 31 written for UTC times, with the exact 1/15 h per degree instead of 0.06667). The zenith angle relation is the standard spherical-trigonometry identity; the incidence angle on a tilted plane is CANDIDATA (form from solar engineering texts; primary reference and its use in Allen et al., 2007, to be verified). The precision of the FAO-56 calendar formulae against a higher-precision ephemeris has not been quantified (decision RC-04).

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

See also

Other radiation functions: ef_atm_emissivity(), ef_net_radiation(), ef_rl_in(), ef_rl_out(), ef_rs_in(), ef_tau_sw()

Examples

deg <- pi / 180
# Horizontal pixel in central Chile, 15 January, 14:30 UTC
ef_solar_geometry(doy = 15, utc_hour = 14.5, lat = -35 * deg,
                  lon = -71 * deg)
#> $cos_zenith
#> [1] 0.8267324
#> 
#> $cos_incidence
#> [1] 0.8267324
#> 
#> $declination
#> [1] -0.3702158
#> 
#> $hour_angle
#> [1] -0.6252064
#> 
#> $inv_distance
#> [1] 1.031906
#> 

# North- and south-facing 20 degree slopes at the same instant
geo <- ef_solar_geometry(doy = 15, utc_hour = 14.5, lat = -35 * deg,
                         lon = -71 * deg, slope = 20 * deg,
                         aspect = c(0, 180) * deg)
geo$cos_incidence
#> [1] 0.8237953 0.7299534

# MOD11A1 view time (local mean solar time, h) converted to UTC first
lon_deg <- -71
view_time <- 10.6
utc_hour <- (view_time - lon_deg / 15) %% 24
ef_solar_geometry(doy = 15, utc_hour = utc_hour, lat = -35 * deg,
                  lon = lon_deg * deg)$cos_zenith
#> [1] 0.9087903
